pr_title: fix: avoid integer overflow in offsets_to_groups when bigidx is enabled
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/11782

1. I have no rust background, so make sure this is the correct fix
2. I assume the reason this bug wasn't caught is that no testing is done for bigidx builds. Is that something worth exploring? Since `polars-u64-idx` builds are published on pypi, I was assuming some level of testing was done.

issue_context.title: `list.eval` broken on main for `bigidx`: `called Option::unwrap() on a None value`
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

Broken on main, works in 0.19.8. Example from `list.eval` docs.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [1, 8, 3], "b": [4, 5, 2]})
df.with_columns(
    pl.concat_list(["a", "b"]).list.eval(pl.element().rank()).alias("rank")
)
```

comments: I don't know if I missed anything, but I didn't reproduce this on the latest main branch. Could you provide the commit hash?

`89ffd882f` works for me without `bigidx`, but fails with the above error when I repeat the same build procedure after adding `bigidx` to the list of features in `py-polars/Cargo.toml`.

Just to make sure I'm not doing anything wrong, this is exactly what I'm doing (within a conda env):
```shell
rustup update
rustup default nightly
git clone https://github.com/pola-rs/polars.git
cd polars/polars-rs
# add bigidx to py-polars/Cargo.toml (under dependencies.polars.features, line 86)
RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native" CFLAGS="-I$CONDA_PREFIX/include" python -m pip install . -vv
cd .. # otherwise I get a polars binary not found warning
python # and run above example code
```

Ah, I think I know what's happening.

`IdxSize::MAX as i64` is `-1` with `IdxSize = u64` (bigidx), so `offsets_to_groups` is returning `None`.
https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/d9c63161fa62ac67b560e40e5a85a6ee8c559a9b/crates/polars-lazy/src/dsl/list.rs#L23-L40

review_comments:
I don't have 2\*\*32 rows but I do have 100M rows with ~1000 list elements each, which triggers an error in non-bigidx builds... I assume because IdxSize is used for list offsets, and I do have more than 2\*\*32 list elements.

I'm also realizing that my fix is dumb because the check is always true. I pushed a slightly less dumb fix but I'll defer to you on the best way to fix it :)

And to clarify, the issue isn't that `(end - start) <= IdxSize::MAX` fails, it's that `IdxSize::MAX as i64` is `-1` when `IdxSize` is `u64` (integer overflow), thus making the inequality always false.
